r: The wobbly Italian cream, flavoured with vanilla, with a berry coulis.
Soften the gelatine in cold water.
Heat the cream with 60 g of sugar and the split vanilla pod, without boiling.|Cooking|5
Take off the heat, add the squeezed gelatine and stir.
Pour into glasses and leave to set in the fridge for 4 h.
Blend the berries with the rest of the sugar and pour over just before serving.
A very gentle panna cotta under an exotic mango coulis.
Soften the gelatine in cold water.
Heat the cream with the sugar without boiling, then add the squeezed gelatine.|Cooking|5
Pour into glasses and leave to set in the fridge for 4 h.
Blend the mango with the lime juice and pour over the panna cottas.
Coconut milk replaces some of the cream.
A lighter panna cotta with a coconut flavour.
Soften the gelatine in cold water.
Heat the coconut milk, cream and sugar, then add the squeezed gelatine.|Cooking|5
Pour into glasses and leave to set in the fridge for 4 h.
Serve with the pineapple cut into small dice.
Poached meringues on a custard, with a drizzle of caramel.
Heat the milk with the split vanilla pod. Whisk the yolks with 80 g of sugar.
Pour the hot milk over the yolks, then thicken over a low heat without boiling, stirring. It is ready when the custard coats the spoon.|Cooking|10
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks with a pinch of salt and 40 g of sugar.
Poach spoonfuls of the whites for 1 min on each side in simmering water.|Cooking|2
Make a caramel with the rest of the sugar and 2 tbsp of water.
Put the meringues on the cold custard and drizzle with caramel.
The whites cook in the microwave in a few seconds.
The quick version, with shop-bought custard.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, adding the sugar at the end.
Spoon 4 mounds of whites into lightly oiled cups.
Cook them in the microwave for 30 seconds.
Turn out onto the custard and drizzle with caramel.
The floating island from Lyon, crunchy and pink.
Make the custard: pour the hot vanilla milk over the yolks whisked with 80 g of sugar, then thicken over a low heat.|Cooking|10
Leave to cool in the fridge.
Whisk the whites with the rest of the sugar.
Poach the whites for 1 min on each side in simmering water.|Cooking|2
Put them on the custard and sprinkle with crushed pralines.
Choux buns filled with vanilla ice cream, covered with hot chocolate sauce.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Bring 12 cl of water, the butter and a pinch of salt to the boil.
Tip in the flour all at once and stir until the dough comes away from the pan.
Off the heat, beat in the eggs one by one.
Pipe small mounds on a baking tray and bake for 25 min without opening the oven.|Oven|25
Melt the chocolate in the hot cream.
Cut the cold buns open, fill them with ice cream and cover with the hot sauce.
Filled with whipped cream, no ice cream.
Light choux buns filled with homemade whipped cream.
Make the choux pastry: bring water, butter and salt to the boil, add the flour all at once, then beat in the eggs one by one.
Pipe small mounds on a baking tray and bake for 25 min at 200 °C.|Oven|25
Whip the very cold cream with the icing sugar.
Fill the cold buns and dust with icing sugar.
Covered with a salted butter caramel sauce.
Profiteroles with a salted butter caramel instead of chocolate.
Make the choux pastry and bake the buns for 25 min at 200 °C.|Oven|25
Melt the sugar on its own until it is a light caramel.
Off the heat, add the hot cream, then the salted butter.
Fill the buns with ice cream and cover with the warm caramel.
Chopped seasonal fruit with a light lemon syrup.
Squeeze the lemon and mix the juice with the sugar.
Peel the oranges, removing all the pith, and cut into pieces.
Dice the apples, pears and bananas.
Mix all the fruit with the grapes and the sweet juice.
A sunny fruit salad with tropical fruit.
Peel the mango, pineapple and kiwis, and cut into dice.
Pour over the lime juice and the passion fruit pulp.
A summer salad with strawberries, raspberries and mint.
Wash and hull the strawberries, then cut them in half.
Mix them with the raspberries and blueberries.
Pour over the lemon juice mixed with the sugar.
Add the chopped mint and chill for 15 min.
Very simple homemade compote, with just apples and a little cinnamon.
Peel and core the apples and cut them into pieces.
Put them in a pan with 10 cl of water, the sugar and the cinnamon.
Cook for 20 min with the lid on, stirring from time to time.|Cooking|20
Mash with a fork or blend, depending on the texture you like.
Half apples, half pears, with no added sugar.
A gentle compote, sweetened only by the fruit.
Peel and core the fruit and cut into pieces.
Put it in a pan with 5 cl of water and the cinnamon.
Cook for 20 min with the lid on.|Cooking|20
Mash or blend, then leave to cool.
With strawberries added at the end of cooking.
A pink, fruity compote that kids love.
Peel the apples and cut them into pieces.
Cook them for 15 min with the lid on, with 5 cl of water and the sugar.|Cooking|15
Add the hulled strawberries and cook for 5 min.|Cooking|5
The vanilla set custard, covered with its light caramel.
Make a caramel with 100 g of sugar and 3 tbsp of water, and pour it into the bottom of the ramekins.
Heat the milk with the split vanilla pod.
Whisk the eggs and the rest of the sugar, then pour the hot milk over them.
Fill the ramekins and bake in a bain-marie for 40 min.|Oven|40
Leave to cool, then chill for 2 h before turning out.
Coconut milk replaces some of the milk.
A set custard with the taste of the islands.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C and make a caramel with 100 g of sugar and a little water.
Pour it into the bottom of the ramekins.
Whisk the eggs with the rest of the sugar, then add the coconut milk and the milk.
Fill the ramekins and bake in a bain-marie for 40 min.|Oven|40
Chill for 2 h before turning out.
Crème caramel without turning on the oven.
Make a caramel with 100 g of sugar and a little water, and pour it into ramekins.
Whisk the eggs, the rest of the sugar and the vanilla sugar, then add the hot milk.
Fill the ramekins and cover them with foil.
Put them in the pressure cooker with 2 cm of water and cook for 6 min after it starts to whistle.|Cooking|6
Leave to cool, then chill for 2 h.
Pears poached in vanilla syrup, covered with hot chocolate.
Bring 1 litre of water to the boil with the sugar and the split vanilla pod.
Peel the pears, leaving the stalk on, and poach them in the syrup for 20 min.|Cooking|20
Leave them to cool in the syrup.
Melt the chocolate in the hot cream.
Serve each pear with a scoop of ice cream and the chocolate sauce.
Red, fragrant pears for a winter dessert.
Bring the wine to the boil with the sugar, cinnamon and orange zest.
Peel the pears, leaving the stalk on.
Poach them for 30 min in the simmering wine, turning them over.|Cooking|30
Remove the pears and boil the wine down to a syrup.|Cooking|10
Serve warm or cold, covered with syrup.
Roasted in the oven with honey, with no syrup.
Cut the pears in half and remove the cores.
Put them in a dish, drizzle with honey and dot with butter and cinnamon.
Bake for 25 min, basting halfway through.|Oven|25
Sponge fingers around a light strawberry mousse.
Soften the gelatine in cold water. Blend half the strawberries with the sugar.
Warm a little of this coulis and melt the gelatine in it, then mix with the rest.
Whip the cream and fold it into the fromage blanc and the coulis.
Quickly dip the sponge fingers in sugar water and line a tin.
Layer the mousse and chopped strawberries, then cover with sponge fingers.
Leave to set in the fridge for 6 h before turning out.
Soften the gelatine. Blend half the raspberries with the sugar and melt the gelatine in a little warm coulis.
Whip the cream and fold it into the fromage blanc and the coulis.
Line a tin with sponge fingers dipped in sugar water.
Layer the mousse and whole raspberries, then cover with sponge fingers.
Leave to set in the fridge for 6 h.
The charlotte for those with a sweet tooth, filled with chocolate mousse.
Melt the chocolate and leave to cool slightly, then add the egg yolks.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks with the sugar and gently fold them into the chocolate.
Quickly dip the sponge fingers in the milk and line a tin.
Pour in the mousse and cover with sponge fingers.
Leave to set in the fridge for 6 h before turning out.
A meringue that is crisp outside and soft inside, with whipped cream and berries.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, then add the sugar little by little until you have a glossy meringue.
Add the cornflour and vinegar, and shape into a big disc on a baking tray.
Bake for 1 h 30, then leave to cool in the switched-off oven.|Oven|90
Whip the cream, spread it over the meringue and top with the berries.
With mango, kiwi and passion fruit.
The pavlova with tropical fruit, fresh and tangy.
Preheat the oven to 120 °C. Whisk the whites with the sugar into a glossy meringue, then add the cornflour.
Shape into a disc on a baking tray and bake for 1 h 30.|Oven|90
Leave to cool in the switched-off oven.
Cover with whipped cream, diced mango and kiwi, then the passion fruit pulp.
Little strawberry pavlovas, to serve on plates.
Preheat the oven to 120 °C. Whisk the whites with the sugar into a meringue, then add the cornflour.
Shape 6 little nests on a baking tray.
Bake for 1 h and leave to cool in the oven.|Oven|60
Fill with whipped cream and sliced strawberries.
The puff pastry galette filled with frangipane, with the charm hidden inside.
Mix the ground almonds, sugar, soft butter and 2 eggs.
Roll out one pastry on a baking tray, spread with frangipane leaving a 2 cm border, and place the charm.
Cover with the second pastry and seal the edges well.
Brush with the last beaten egg and draw patterns with the tip of a knife.
Compote and apples instead of frangipane.
A lighter galette, filled with apples.
Roll out one pastry, spread with compote, then add thin apple slices sprinkled with sugar, and place the charm.
Cover with the second pastry and seal the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30 min.|Oven|30
Chocolate and pear galette des rois
Chocolate frangipane and pieces of pear.
The chocolate and pear duo, in a galette des rois.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Melt the chocolate.
Mix the ground almonds, sugar, butter, 2 eggs and the melted chocolate.
Roll out one pastry, spread with frangipane and diced pears, and place the charm.
Cover with the second pastry, seal the edges and brush with the last egg.
